question_text: [Exploratory Data Analysis & Feature Engineering - Q32] In multiple linear regression, what does a Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) score greater than 10 for a feature indicate?

options.text: The feature has zero explanatory power
Severe multicollinearity, meaning the feature's variance is largely explained by a linear combination of other features
The residual errors follow a Poisson distribution

answer_explanation: VIF = 1 / (1 - R^2_i). A VIF > 10 indicates that more than 90% of the variance of feature i is shared with other predictors, inflating coefficient standard errors.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: VIF = 1 / (1 - R^2_i). A VIF > 10 indicates that more than 90% of the variance of feature i is shared with other predictors, inflating coefficient standard errors.
